title: Design a Hotel Booking System: Hotel, Room types, Reservation, Guest, check-in/check-out, search by date/location/price, cancellation policy.
topicTitle: LLD Problems: Parking Lot, Elevator, Chess, etc.
keyPoints: The hardest part is date-range availability: a room is available only if no existing reservation overlaps the requested dates.
Overlap is checked with the standard condition: one range starts before the other ends and vice versa.
A Hotel owns rooms grouped by RoomType (standard, deluxe, suite), each with a nightly price.
A Reservation moves through a lifecycle: CONFIRMED, CHECKED_IN, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED.
Cancellation is isolated behind a CancellationPolicy interface so the business can switch between free-until-24h and tiered penalties.
Concurrency is critical: two guests booking the last room for overlapping dates must be serialised with an atomic check-and-reserve.
This maps directly to reserving vault lockers at National Bank of India for a date range.

s1_definition.oneliner: A hotel system reserves a typed room for a guest over a date range and manages the booking lifecycle with a cancellation policy.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Hotel** – owns rooms grouped by `RoomType` (standard, deluxe, suite), each with a nightly price.
- **Room** – has a room number, type, and a method to check availability against existing reservations.
- **Reservation** – holds a room for a guest over a date range, progressing through CONFIRMED, CHECKED_IN, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED.
- **Guest** – the person making the reservation.
- **CancellationPolicy** – a pluggable interface for free-until-24h, tiered penalties, or no-refund policies.
- **Date-range availability** – the central algorithmic challenge, using overlap detection.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of booking a hotel room like reserving a bank locker for a date range at National Bank of India. Rajesh reserves a deluxe locker from the 1st to the 5th. While reserved, no one else can take that exact locker for overlapping dates. He checks in, uses it, checks out, and if he cancels early the bank applies a cancellation fee based on how late he cancelled.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Reservation Lifecycle:
  ──────────────────────

  CONFIRMED ──checkIn──→ CHECKED_IN ──checkOut──→ COMPLETED
       │
       └──cancel──→ CANCELLED (apply penalty)
```

```text
  Date-Range Overlap Detection:
  ─────────────────────────────

  Existing:   |───────────|
              checkIn    checkOut

  Request A:       |────|           → overlaps (conflict)
  Request B:                |────|  → no overlap (OK)
  Request C:  |────|                → no overlap (OK)

  Overlap condition: a.start < b.end && b.start < a.end
```

```text
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │           HotelService                │
  │  search(type, dates)                  │
  │  book(guest, room, dates)             │
  │  cancel(reservation)                  │
  └──────┬──────────────┬────────────────┘
         │              │
         ▼              ▼
  ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────────────┐
  │    Room      │ │ CancellationPolicy │
  │ isAvailable()│ │ computePenalty()   │
  └──────────────┘ └────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When you design a hotel booking system, the hardest and most important piece is date-range availability. A room is available for a requested check-in and check-out only if no existing non-cancelled reservation overlaps those dates, and you test overlap with the standard condition that one range starts before the other ends and vice versa. Getting this exactly right is what prevents double-booking.

The entities are a Hotel that owns rooms grouped by type such as standard, deluxe, and suite each with a nightly price, a Reservation that holds one room for one guest over a date range, and a Guest. A reservation moves through a clear lifecycle: confirmed when booked, checked-in on arrival, completed on departure, or cancelled.

Cancellation is where business rules change constantly, so isolating it behind a cancellation-policy interface is essential. The bank can offer free cancellation up to twenty-four hours before arrival, or a tiered penalty, and switching between them is a new policy class with zero change to the booking service. This is the Open/Closed Principle and Strategy pattern working together.

The concurrency concern is that two guests trying to book the last deluxe room for overlapping dates at the same instant must be serialised, otherwise both succeed and the hotel is oversold. Enforce this with an atomic check-and-reserve, in practice a database constraint or a lock scoped to the room and date range. At National Bank of India, this is identical to reserving a limited physical asset like a vault locker for a date range.

Remember one sentence: a hotel booking system checks date-range overlap atomically, manages a reservation lifecycle, and applies cancellation penalties through a pluggable policy.
